chunks: From him, from Musa ibn 'Umar, from 'Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Hariz, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked: 'Who is the one upon whom I am compelled and whose maintenance is obligatory upon me?' He said: 'The two parents, the child, and the wife.'
ai.seo_question: Who are the relatives upon whom a man is legally obligated to provide financial maintenance in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) explicitly delineates the three primary categories of dependents for whom a man bears mandatory financial maintenance (nafaqah): parents, children, and wife. This concise enumeration serves as a foundational legal principle in Shia jurisprudence, clarifying the scope of familial obligation beyond the general Quranic injunctions. It underscores the structured hierarchy of financial responsibility within the Islamic family unit, ensuring the welfare of both ascending and descending generations as well as the marital bond.
